title: Leny Yoro's red inside ten minutes: obvious chance, or the keeper's ball?
description:
Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United, Anfield, 22 November 2026. Early on, Matthijs de Ligt misjudges a long ball and Alexander Isak is through. Leny Yoro gets back and brings him down just outside the box. Referee Sam Barrott shows a straight red for denying an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO), and VAR checks and confirms it. Dominik Szoboszlai scores the free kick, Florian Wirtz adds a second, and Liverpool score twice more after the break.

Under Law 12, a DOGSO call weighs distance to goal, direction of play, the chance of keeping or gaining control of the ball, and where the defenders are. Reports say Isak's touch was heavy, towards the keeper. The officials judged it still a chance; United's manager and players say it was never a red. That point is disputed, and it is shown as disputed. Reports also differ on the minute (7th, 8th or 9th).

Sources: Premier League (MW11 VAR decisions explained), Evening Standard, The Independent, Sky Sports, Brit Brief. Rebuilt from match reports: positions are illustrative, not to scale. No view taken on the officials.
